newsitem.title: DUBAI: Gulf allies meet on Qatar-Bahrain dispute.
newsitem.headline: Gulf allies meet on Qatar-Bahrain dispute.

text.p: Gulf Arab foreign ministers met in the Saudi Arabian capital Riyadh on Tuesday to try to resolve a border dispute between Bahrain and Qatar, officials said.

Foreign ministers of Qatar and Bahrain arrived in Riyadh to join their counterparts from the other Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) members -- Kuwait, Oman, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) -- who met for talks earlier in the day.

"(Qatari Foreign Minister) Sheikh Hamad bin Jassim bin Jabr al-Thani and (Bahrain's Foreign Minister) Sheikh Mohammad bin Mubarak al-Khalifa are currently having lunch with the four other foreign ministers," one official said.
"After that, they will hold a meeting to present their countries' stands on the issue," he added. It would be the two men's first face-to-face talk on the dispute.
Saudi officials changed the venue of the meeting and banned reporters and cameramen from the heavily guarded gates of the GCC headquarters, where the afternoon talks will be held.
Qatar and Bahrain have been locked for decades in a dispute over a cluster of islands, sandbanks and reefs in the Gulf controlled by Bahrain since the 1930s but also claimed by Qatar.
Qatar has taken the case to the International Court of Justice at The Hague, a move bitterly opposed by Bahrain which insists on an Arab solution.
Ties worsened further after Bahrain put on trial two Qataris for spying and boycotted a GCC summit in December in protest against Qatar's refusal to withdraw the case from The Hague.
Bahrain last month pardoned the two Qataris after a state security court sentenced them to three years in jail for spying.
Tuesday's talks were the first meeting of a committee of foreign ministers of Kuwait, Oman, Saudi Arabia and the UAE set up to resolve the Bahrain-Qatar dispute.
It was scheduled to hold its first meeting in Cairo last month but was postponed at Saudi Arabia's request.
Saudi Defence Minister Prince Sultan told reporters after attending a graduation ceremony at the King Faisal Air Force Academy on Tuesday that he hoped the committee would succeed in its effort.
